title: Add Kubernetes deployment recipe (RAG/agent templates) with OTel collector guidance
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: - Adds a Kubernetes deployment recipe for template-style apps (Deployment/Service/Ingress + optional OTel Collector sidecar)\n- Documents Dedicated/Private notes: networking, auth, and collector/exporter placement\n- Adds a small 'verify telemetry' job manifest and troubleshooting tips
description:
## Summary
This PR adds a Kubernetes deployment recipe intended for the RAG + agent quickstart templates (and other Redwood API-based apps) with production-minded defaults: explicit resource requests/limits, health probes, graceful shutdown, and a recommended OpenTelemetry Collector configuration.

The recipe is written to work for:
- Hosted API customers (standard outbound HTTPS)
- Dedicated customers (same API surface, but emphasizes stable egress + capacity predictability)
- Private/VPC customers (collector/exporter and networking considerations, and how to avoid leaking PII in telemetry)

## What’s included
- `k8s/base/` manifests:
  - `deployment.yaml` (app container, env var schema, probes, terminationGracePeriodSeconds)
  - `service.yaml`
  - `ingress.yaml` (optional; includes notes on corporate proxies and header policies)
  - `configmap.yaml` (non-secret config)
  - `secret.example.yaml` (example only; does not include real values)
- `k8s/otel/` manifests:
  - `collector-config.yaml` (collector pipeline w/ redaction processor notes; minimal attributes to avoid high-cardinality)
  - `collector-deployment.yaml` (as a sidecar option)
  - `collector-daemonset.yaml` (cluster-wide option for larger orgs)
- `k8s/jobs/verify-telemetry.yaml`: a small Job that hits the app endpoint and prints where to look for traces/metrics (meant for local clusters or first-time setup)
- `docs/deploy/kubernetes.md`: step-by-step guide including Dedicated/Private sections and troubleshooting

## Key decisions / rationale
- Collector placement: default docs recommend a sidecar collector for the template apps because it keeps the coupling explicit and makes it easier for teams to see "what telemetry gets emitted" without needing cluster-level privileges. We still document the DaemonSet approach as an alternative for platform teams.
- Cardinality controls: the collector config explicitly avoids putting user IDs, prompt text, or arbitrary tool arguments into attributes. The guide links to our internal conventions around span attributes and calls out which fields must be redacted.
- Secrets: the example uses Kubernetes Secrets + env vars, and explicitly warns against checking secrets into Git. It also includes a note for External Secrets / KMS-backed stores in enterprise clusters.
- Dedicated/Private notes: the guide calls out TLS inspection proxies and header allow-lists (in response to recent proxy issues), and suggests turning off optional template-telemetry tags if an org’s proxy blocks unknown headers.

## Testing
- Rendered manifests via `kustomize build k8s/overlays/dev` and applied to kind cluster locally
- Smoke tested health endpoints (`/healthz`, `/readyz`) and graceful shutdown
- Verified traces reach a local collector + exporter in dev overlay
- Ran lint/markdown checks in CI

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Add a Helm chart wrapper (decide if we want to own it vs keep manifests + kustomize)
- Add a dedicated overlay example for Private deployments where the collector is required to export to an in-network endpoint

Refs: ENG-4184 (observability pack integration), ENG-4189 (request-id propagation), SUP-29422 (exporter auth confusion).

snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redwood-template-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/template-app:latest
          env:
            - name: REDWOOD_API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: redwood-api
                  key: api_key
            - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
              value: http://127.0.0.1:4317
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: 8080
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
        - name: otel-collector
          image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.96.0
          args: ["--config=/etc/otel/collector-config.yaml"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: otel-config
              mountPath: /etc/otel
      volumes:
        - name: otel-config
          configMap:
            name: otel-collector-config
review_conversation:
Allison Grant (review): Collector config looks good overall. Two asks: (1) please remove `http.url` from default span attributes in the example (too easy to accidentally include query params) and (2) call out that tool arguments/tool outputs should never be attributes.

Sabrina James (author): Good call. Removed `http.url` from the docs snippet and added an explicit note under the tracing section that tool args/outputs must be redacted or only logged at DEBUG locally.

Christine Wong (review): Love the probes + termination grace period. Can we add a note about keeping request timeout < ingress idle timeout to avoid half-open streaming connections? Also, can the guide mention what to do if a corporate proxy blocks unknown headers (we’ve seen this).

Sabrina James (author): Added a "Streaming + proxies" subsection: recommends aligning server timeout with ingress/proxy timeouts and mentions disabling optional template telemetry tags if proxies reject unknown headers.

Elliot Price (review): Docs structure: please mirror the template README style (Prereqs -> Deploy -> Verify -> Troubleshooting). Also link to the observability verification script page.

Sabrina James (author): Re-ordered `docs/deploy/kubernetes.md` accordingly and added the link.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI is green. One minor: pin collector image version in manifests (avoid `latest`).

Sabrina James (author): Pinned to `otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.96.0` and added a short note on upgrade cadence + testing.
post_merge_notes: After merge: confirm docs site cross-linking from Quickstarts -> Deployment Recipes includes Kubernetes, and ensure observability-pack dashboard docs references this recipe for collector placement options.
